newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Aid agencies urge access to refugees in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Aid agencies urge access to refugees in Zaire.

text.p: Aid agencies stepped up the pressure on Zaire's Tutsi-dominated rebels on Tuesday to unblock access to Rwandan Hutu refugees facing hunger and disease.
The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR said its work remained paralysed for the second day running after the rebels blocked its staff from entering the camps south of the eastern city of Kisangani.

The U.N. children's agency appealed to President Nelson Mandela of South Africa, which hosted a first round of talks between the rebels and Zaire's government, to intervene with rebel leader Laurent Kabila to help evacuate refugee children.
"As the world watches and waits, hundreds of children are at death's door," UNICEF chief Carol Bellamy said in a statement.

A UNHCR plan to airlift a first group of refugee children from Kisangani has been delayed by mounting rebel bureaucracy, demands for further medical checks on cholera cases in the camps and complaints that the operation will clog the local airport.
UNHCR spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole told a briefing that more than 1,500 Hutus had died from hunger and disease at the camps so far in April and that the death rate was rising slightly.
The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, Sadako Ogata, has accused the rebels of blocking her agency's work.
O'Toole said Ogata on Monday spoke by telephone to Rwandan President Pasteur Bizimungu who promised to back the airlift.
But senior aid officials say privately that Rwanda, Africa's most crowded country swamped after months of coping with Hutu returnees, does not want a large number of refugees coming home.
The Rwandans are the rump of more than two million Hutus who fled in 1994 after the victory of Tutsi rebels in the civil war and the Hutu-led genocide of 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
Most went home late last year, but up to 300,000 fled deeper into Zaire where they have been on the run for five months.
The refugee camps have been attacked by local Zaireans, some of whom say they are being encouraged by the rebels. Aid workers have also become the targets of attacks and looting by locals.

The rebels have requisitioned aviation fuel the UNHCR was hoping to use for the airlift. Aid workers said the rebels also recently seized a ferry the UNHCR was using for the relief operation across the Zaire river south of Kisangani.
Aid officials say the humanitarian operation is in total chaos amid uncertainty over the rebel chain of command on the ground and problems in contacting top officials of Kabila.
